notes.meaning: A person who truly wants to gain wisdom welcomes guidance and correction. Resenting correction shows stubborn foolishness, like an animal that refuses to learn from being guided.
God looks with favor on people who are kind and seek the good of others. At the same time, the Lord brings judgment on those who secretly plan harm against their neighbors.

differ.view: Methodists emphasize that God's grace changes the heart first so a person can become good, and continuing in obedience increases that goodness and God's favor.

notes.meaning: Sinful behavior might seem to bring quick success, but it cannot build a lasting life. Godly people stay secure because their lives are deeply rooted in God, like strong trees that a storm cannot pull up.
A wife of strong, noble character brings great honor and joy to her husband, like a royal crown. But a wife who acts dishonorably drains his strength and eats away his peace from the inside.
The inner goals of the righteous are fair and guided by God's standard of justice. In contrast, the schemes of wicked people are full of trickery and aim to take advantage of others.
Evil people use their words like a deadly trap to hurt or destroy innocent people. Good people speak up honestly and bravely, using their words to defend and rescue those under attack.
Sinners may seem powerful for a time, but when trouble strikes, their whole world collapses. God protects the families of the righteous, giving them a firm home that stands for generations.
People earn lasting respect when they show true, practical wisdom in how they live. But anyone with a crooked, scheming mind will end up being despised by both God and wise people.

An ordinary, humble worker who can quietly support his household is far better off than an arrogant person. Some people boast of family status or wear fancy clothes to look grand, while having nothing to eat at home.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates this verse as praising a poor man who provides for himself over a proud man who lacks bread.

notes.meaning: A godly person shows kindness even to working animals, making sure they have enough rest and food. By contrast, the so-called kindness of cruel people is still harsh and self-serving.
A person who works hard at an honest job will have plenty of food for the table. But wasting time on empty schemes and idle companions leads straight to poverty and shows poor judgment.
Wicked people always envy the loot and dishonest tricks of other evil men. Meanwhile, the righteous draw strength from God within, bearing good fruit naturally without needing to rob anyone.
Sinners often get caught in their own web of lies, insults, and careless speech. Upright people avoid that danger because their honest words keep them out of legal and personal trouble.
Good and helpful words bring real blessings back to the one who speaks them. In the same way, honest work done with our hands receives a good reward from God.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that God rewarding human works does not mean people earn salvation by their own merit, but shows God's gracious kindness in accepting good works through Christ.

notes.meaning: A fool is always convinced that his own opinion and way of doing things cannot be wrong. A truly wise person remains humble enough to seek out advice and listen to others.
A foolish person flares up quickly and lets everyone see his temper the moment he feels slighted. A sensible person stays calm, holds his temper, and overlooks an insult rather than starting a brawl.
When an honest person speaks the truth, he helps establish justice and fair treatment for all. A dishonest witness lies freely, spreading deception and causing harm in the community.
Thoughtless and cruel words can cut deeply into a person's spirit, just like wounds from a sword. But words spoken with wisdom and gentleness bring peace and heal broken relationships.
Truth stands the test of time because it never changes and cannot be destroyed. Lies may work for a brief moment, but they are quickly found out and exposed.
Those who secretly plan harm to others end up trapped in their own deceit and misery. On the other hand, people who work to make peace bring joy both to their neighbors and to their own hearts.
God watches over the upright so that real and final harm will not ruin their souls. Trouble may come, but God turns it for their ultimate good, whereas the wicked face ruin from their sins.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that no punishment for sin will ever fall on the righteous, because Christ bore all their punishment in their place.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates this proverb to mean that nothing that happens will cause lasting sadness to a just person.

notes.meaning: The Lord deeply hates lying words because falsehood opposes his holy nature. But he takes great delight in people who speak the truth and keep their promises faithfully.
Sensible people do not show off everything they know just to impress a crowd. But fools cannot help blurting out whatever nonsense comes into their heads, showing off their ignorance.
Hardworking and reliable people naturally rise to positions of leadership and respect. Lazy people, however, waste their opportunities and eventually find themselves forced to work for others.
Worry and sadness can crush a person's spirit and make life feel too heavy to carry. An encouraging, kind word can lift that burden and fill the heart with fresh hope.
Upright people are careful about their companions and guide their neighbors toward what is good. Evil people, however, wander down bad roads and drag others into ruin with them.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that the righteous person is more excellent than his neighbor because he has been clothed in the perfect righteousness of Christ.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates the first line to mean that a righteous person is someone who willingly accepts a loss for the sake of a friend.

notes.meaning: A lazy hunter does not even bother to prepare and cook what he catches, letting his hard-earned food go to waste. But a diligent person values what he owns and makes good use of every blessing.
Walking in obedience to God brings true, lasting life and spiritual safety. This righteous way leads away from destruction and toward God's eternal peace.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates the second line as a contrast, saying that the by-way leads directly to death.
